text.text: Outbound: how does the draft claim suppress a concurrent double Send?
New engineers · Two Today tabs sending one draft, the Next.js server action, and the conditional Postgres claim on its row.

Local client: two tabs, one
session

DraftCard Send with
the edited text

Same draft, second
tab; same Send call

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient,
response included; solid = sync. Flow type is also written on each arrow.
The claim is one conditional UPDATE

UPDATE sets sending, clears error,
stamps sentAt/updatedAt, saves edits
WHERE id, out, status IN (draft,failed)
RETURNING. A concurrent UPDATE
then matches 0 rows → skipped.

Winner's outcome arrives after
guards/delivery. Throws and most
guards set failed, claimable again,
even if markSent throws after Gmail
accepted; closed/replied set skipped.
Crash after claim strands the row

If the function dies after the claim, the
row stays 'sending': Send/Skip match
only draft|failed; refresh only resolves
LinkedIn rows with a run id. Today
shows it 'Queued on LinkedIn'.

Outside this view: Guards and Gmail/LinkedIn/X delivery that run after a successful claim; Conversation Send: each click inserts its own row, so no
shared claim.
